papers.title_in_file: Multivariable QSP and Bosonic Quantum Simulation using Iterated Quantum Signal Processing
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper that chains quantum signal processing sequences to build multivariate polynomials and to simulate bosonic Hamiltonians.

assertions.value: The authors state that iterated quantum signal processing applies quantum signal processing recursively to the outputs of other quantum signal processing steps, which lets polynomials be achieved that would otherwise be difficult to find analytically.
quotes: This method recursively applies quantum signal processing to the outputs of other quantum signal processing steps, allowing polynomials to be easily achieved that would otherwise be difficult to find analytically.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own construction, stated in the abstract; no formal theorem is cited here.

assertions.value: The authors state that they use iterated QSP to implement the complex arithmetic of bosonic Hamiltonian simulation using only two ancillary qubits, by taking advantage of the sparsity.
quotes: we take advantage of the sparsity and use iterated QSP to implement the complex arithmetic using only two ancillary qubits.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' stated construction; the paper gives no hardware run.

assertions.value: The authors state that their methods do not scale favorably with the degree of the polynomial, and that further work is needed to learn whether the limit is fundamental.
quotes: as the degree of the polynomial increases the methods that we propose do not scale favorably with the degree of the polynomial considered
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state their own limit in the Conclusion.

papers.title_in_file: Materials Discovery With Quantum-Enhanced Machine Learning Algorithms
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction summary, Section V Conclusions
papers.what_it_is: A Pasqal and Panasonic study that applies two quantum-enhanced extremal learning algorithms (QEL and FM+QAOA) to heteroacene discovery, run by noiseless emulation.

assertions.value: The authors report that the training sets held 54, 99 and 119 molecules encoded with N = 7, 16 and 22 bits, and that both algorithms extrapolated to heteroacene structures with lower reorganization energy than in the initial dataset.
quotes: to construct three initial training datasets containing 54, 99 and 119 molecules encoded using N = 7, 16 and 22 bits, respectively.
assertions.certainty_reason: One study with numerical experiments.
assertions.reader_inference: The abstract sentence on extrapolation prints with a lost symbol, so the quote holds the dataset setup only.

assertions.value: The authors report that FM+QAOA, applied to the N = 22 dataset, predicted a compound (octacene) already in the first iteration.
quotes: FM+QAOA was also applied to a larger dataset with N = 22, predicting a compound (octacene) with
assertions.certainty_reason: One study; the energy figure sits in a symbol-bearing sentence, so the quote holds the setup only.

assertions.value: The authors state that the numerical results were computed by noiseless emulation on large classical computing resources.
quotes: The numerical results presented in this work were computed via noiseless emulation on large classical computing resources.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup in the Conclusions.

papers.title_in_file: OnionVQE Optimization Strategy for Ground State Preparation on NISQ Devices
papers.what_it_is: A Bosch paper that proposes a layer-wise identity initialization and shallow ansatz for VQE on a cuprate model Hamiltonian.

assertions.value: The authors report that OnionVQE generates ground state approximations with fidelity values above 0.94 for all the systems studied, with shallow circuit depths.
quotes: generates good ground state approximations (achieving fidelity values above 0.94 for all the systems studied) with shallow circuit depths and a small number of gates.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation result for the systems in this one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that on IBM's FakeMumbai the energy error rose approximately tenfold relative to a noiseless statevector simulator.
quotes: observed an approximately tenfold increase in energy error when compared to the results from a noiseless statevector simulator
assertions.certainty_reason: Noisy simulator (FakeMumbai), not hardware.

assertions.value: The authors state that OnionVQE reaches chemical accuracy of 0.0016 Ha only for the 4- and 6-qubit systems on the statevector simulator.
quotes: The OnionVQE algorithm achieves chemical accuracy of 0.0016 Ha [4] only for our 4- and 6-qubit systems on the statevector simulator.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state their own limit.

papers.title_in_file: Critical point search and linear response theory for computing electronic excitation energies of molecular systems. Part I
papers.what_it_is: A classical electronic-structure theory paper on Kahler manifolds, critical point search and linear response for Hartree-Fock and DFT.
papers.why_not: Classical excited-state quantum chemistry theory; it has no quantum computing or machine learning workload.

papers.title_in_file: GSQAS: Graph Self-supervised Quantum Architecture Search
papers.what_it_is: A paper that pre-trains a graph encoder on unlabeled quantum circuits to train a predictor for quantum architecture search.

assertions.value: The authors report that GSQAS outperforms the state-of-the-art predictor-based QAS, with better performance from fewer labeled circuits, in simulations on variational quantum eigensolver and quantum state classification.
quotes: Simulation results on searching circuit structures for variational quantum eigensolver and quantum state classification show that GSQAS outperforms the state-of-the-art predictor-based QAS, achieving better performance with fewer labeled circuits.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation results from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that GSQAS first pre-trains a graph encoder on a large number of unlabeled quantum circuits using a pretext task, then trains the downstream predictor on a small number of circuit representations and their labels.
quotes: we first pre-train a graph encoder on a large number of unlabeled quantum circuits using a well-designed pretext task in order to generate meaningful representations of circuits.
Then the downstream predictor is trained on a small number of quantum circuits' representations and their labels.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own method.

assertions.value: The authors state that the simulations cover the variational quantum eigensolver and variational quantum classifier tasks, and that other variational algorithms such as quantum compiling and QAOA are left to future work.
quotes: The simulations on variational quantum eigensolver and variational quantum classifier illustrate the superiority of the proposed graph encoding scheme and the self-supervised pre-training.

In future work, we will design other pretext tasks to pre-train the encoder and apply GSQAS to other variational quantum algorithms, e.g., quantum compiling and quantum approximate optimization algorithms.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope.

papers.title_in_file: Probabilistic Quantum SVM Training on Ising Machine
papers.what_it_is: A paper that trains SVMs as QUBO problems on a Coherent Ising Machine with a Boltzmann-distribution probabilistic approach and batch ensembles.

assertions.value: The authors report that on the banknote binary dataset their CIM-based QSVM achieved up to 20% higher accuracy than the original QSVM, while training up to 104 times faster than simulated annealing methods.
quotes: On the banknote binary classification dataset, our CIM-based QSVM, utilizing an energy-based probabilistic approach, achieved up to 20% higher accuracy compared to the original QSVM, while training up to 104 times faster than simulated annealing methods.
assertions.certainty_reason: One empirical study on small datasets.

assertions.value: The authors report that, compared with classical SVM, their approach either matched or reduced training time.
quotes: Compared with classical SVM, our approach either matched or reduced training time.
assertions.certainty_reason: One empirical study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the limited qubit count in contemporary quantum devices constrains training on larger datasets, and that current quantum devices still face limitations in qubit counts and error rates.
quotes: Additionally, the limited qubit count in contemporary quantum devices constrains training on larger datasets.
current quantum devices still face limitations in qubit counts and error rates.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state the limit of the setting.

papers.title_in_file: Potential of quantum scientific machine learning applied to weather modelling
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Section VI Conclusion and Outlook
papers.what_it_is: A Pasqal and BASF paper that uses parameterised quantum circuits for supervised stream function learning and for solving the barotropic vorticity equation with differentiable quantum circuits.

assertions.value: The authors report that a quantum model was trained to accurately reproduce real-world global stream function dynamics at a resolution of 4 degrees, and that the BVE was solved with the differentiable quantum circuits algorithm.
quotes: we demonstrate how a quantum model can be trained to accurately reproduce real-world global stream function dynamics at a resolution of 4
assertions.certainty_reason: One simulated study; the degree sign prints as a lost symbol, so the quote is cut before it.

assertions.value: The authors state that no conclusive quantum advantage can be inferred from the results, and that there is still a large gap to state-of-the-art classical ML solutions.
quotes: Even though no conclusive quantum advantage can be inferred from the results presented here
It is clear of course that there is still a large gap to stateof-the-art classical ML solutions
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state their own limit.

assertions.value: The authors state that the barotropic vorticity equation is the highest order non-linear PDE to be tackled with the DQC algorithm to date.
quotes: it is the highest order non-linear PDE to be tackled with the DQC algorithm to date.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' claim of priority; no survey is cited.

papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Sections 2-4 headings and Theorems 10, 20, 25, 26 statements
papers.what_it_is: A quantum query complexity paper that samples an edge on an s-t path and applies it to path finding and cut-set finding.

assertions.value: The authors state that an edge on a path between s and t can be sampled with query complexity asymptotically the same, up to log factors, as that of detecting a path between s and t.
quotes: show that this can be done in query complexity that is asymptotically the same, up to log factors, as the query complexity of detecting a path between s and t.
assertions.certainty_reason: Main result of the paper, proved in Sections 3 and 4.

assertions.value: The paper proves for n-vertex complete graphs with a promised path of length L that st-edge can be solved in O(n L) expected quantum queries.
quotes: Then st-edgeG(x) can be solved in O(n L) expected quantum queries on input x
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 20 is a proved result.

assertions.value: The authors state that their main technical contribution is an algorithm for generating a quantum state proportional to the positive witness vector of a span program.
quotes: Our main technical contribution is an algorithm for generating a quantum state that is proportional to the positive witness vector of a span program.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own contribution (Theorem 10).
